items.item_text: Background Check: Continued employment is contingent upon the completion of a satisfactory background investigation.
Age Requirement: Candidate(s) must be 18 years or older to be eligible to be hired.
Master's Degree or an equivalent combination of education and experience.
Bachelor's Degree in related area and / or equivalent experience / training.
3-5 years of relevant work experience, or an equivalent combination of education and experience.

Under the general supervision of the Faculty Director, the Research and Policy Project Analyst independently coordinates and manages research and policy initiatives for Million Dollar Hoods. The position develops and monitors project plans, timelines and deliverables; coordinates internal and external stakeholders; contributes to research and policy analysis; identifies and resolves project-related issues; prepares project reports and summaries; and serves as a primary point of contact for assigned initiatives. The position works collaboratively with faculty, community partners, researchers, and other stakeholders to advance project objectives. The Research and Policy Project Analyst will be responsible for managing the various initiatives of MDH. Project management in these positions involves coordinating meetings between stakeholders, setting and facilitating agendas and discussions when needed, setting timelines, and monitoring progress by team members on various tasks. The ideal candidate will be a primary point of contact which requires learning the past and present activities as well as the future direction of the respective initiatives, and being able to publicly speak on behalf of the projects.
Demonstrated proficiency with Microsoft office suite, Google Suite, and other software programs.
Interpersonal skills to develop cordial and cooperative working relationships with University administrators and staff.
Knowledge of the Million Dollar Hoods, Luskin School of Public Affairs & Bunche Center’s goals and objectives.

Demonstrated excellent interpersonal, verbal, and written communications skills to interact effectively and diplomatically with faculty, university administrators, staff, students, and off-campus professionals.
A working knowledge of LA County government structure and the history of movements in Black LA communities.
Writing skills to present ideas in a logical and concise manner.
Ability to think clearly and logically with frequent interruptions and changing priorities.

Oral communications skills to serve as a liaison to convey a variety of information concisely and accurately.Skills to interact in a competent manner with colleagues, community members, and outside organization officials and staff from diverse social, cultural, and educational backgrounds.
Demonstrated ability in working independently and following tasks through to completion.Skill in defining problems and proposing solutions.

Demonstrated project management skills, including developing project plans, establishing timelines and deliverables, coordinating multiple stakeholders, monitoring progress, identifying risks or barriers, and resolving project-related issues.
Demonstrated ability to evaluate programs, policies, or projects and develop sound conclusions and recommendations.
